name: Unbilled Work Review Queue
value_proposition: Turn a job or time-entry export into a skip-ruled unbilled queue with oldest-first ranking and field-limited invoice outlines — the owner creates or holds each invoice, and the kit never sends, collects, or records a payment.
persona: Owner of a contractor, agency, clinic, or professional-services firm that completes jobs or time entries in a tracker and invoices later from QuickBooks, Xero, or a spreadsheet, and who currently finds unbilled work only when cash feels tight.
problem: Work is done and not invoiced. Time entries sit in draft, completed jobs have no invoice number, and retainers are not drawn. Collections chases invoices that already went out; this catches work that never became an invoice.
workflow: 1. The person writes skip rules before any outline: already invoiced (invoice id present), owner-marked write-off or warranty, below the owner's minimum, dates after the as-of date, and disputed jobs. PERSON DECIDES: the minimum amount, which statuses are never billed, and which jobs or customers are always skipped.

2. The person exports completed jobs or time entries as CSV with job or entry id, customer, date completed or worked, amount or hours and rate, invoice status, and invoice id if any, plus the export's as-of date. They open last week's billing log. PERSON DECIDES: which columns to keep. Remove emails, phone numbers, and any columns the workflow does not need. This is an export review, not a live QuickBooks, Xero, time-tracker, or invoicing-tool connection.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to paste the rows as text, upload a file, or not use AI for this data at all.
4. The person pastes the Unbilled Queue Prompt and their rules from the Skip Rules and Minimum Worksheet, then attaches or pastes the export and the billing log.

5. AI runs SKIP RULES FIRST. It sets aside already-invoiced rows (invoice id present), warranty or write-off statuses, amounts below the owner's minimum, dates after the as-of date, and disputed jobs. Every skipped row is listed with its reason. PERSON DECIDES: whether a warranty, write-off, or disputed row should still be billed.

6. AI ranks remaining unbilled rows by oldest completion date first, then by amount (or hours x owner rate if amount is missing). It drafts an invoice outline using only export fields: customer, id, date, hours, rate, and amount. It does not invent line items, taxes, or terms. PERSON DECIDES: whether hours, rate, and amount are complete enough to outline.

7. AI labels CONFIRMED (from the export or log), NEEDS YOUR CHECK (missing rate, customer, amount, or id), AI INTERPRETATION (a blank invoice id is not proof the customer was never billed off-export), and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. PERSON DECIDES: whether each recommended action happens.

8. The person uses the Invoice Outline Review Checklist and checks every CONFIRMED number against the export row. PERSON DECIDES: create, hold, or write off each row in their own invoicing tool. The Blueprint never sends an invoice, records a payment, or edits QuickBooks or Xero. Outcomes (invoiced, hold, write-off) go in the billing log and feed next week's run.
before: The owner invoices whichever job they remember on Sunday night. Completed work from two weeks ago stays unbilled until someone asks for a statement.
after: Each week the owner reviews an unbilled queue with skip reasons and invoice outlines whose numbers match the export. Already-invoiced and write-off rows stay out. The owner still creates or holds each invoice in their own billing tool.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/unbilled-work-review-queue using a fictional four-row job export dated as of 2026-05-11, with a fictional owner minimum of $150. SKIP RULES FIRST skips J-91 (invoice_id INV-220), J-70 (warranty), and J-94 (below $150). The ranked unbilled queue has one row, J-88 Northgate Clinic, oldest first, with an outline whose hours, rate, and amount match the export. A fact-check shows Matches. Next week's billing log skips J-88 after it is marked invoiced as INV-241. The demo ends on the owner creating the invoice. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone. Every job, customer, amount, and date is invented. No live QuickBooks, Xero, or time-tracker connection is attached.

List J-94 as SKIPPED with text containing '$85' and '$150'. Show that disputed jobs and dates after the as-of date are also skip rules even when this export has no such row.

Step 3 of 6 - The ranked unbilled queue: show exactly 1 queued row, J-88, as oldest remaining completion date first. Show CONFIRMED text containing 'Northgate Clinic', 'J-88', '2026-04-22', '12', '85', and '1020'. Show the invoice outline 'Northgate Clinic, J-88, 12 hours at $85, $1,020, date 2026-04-22'. Show the exact sentence 'Do not add tax or terms not in the export.' Show the text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'NEEDS YOUR CHECK', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as visible words, not as color or icon alone. Show AI INTERPRETATION text containing 'blank invoice id' and 'does not prove'. Show that a row with no customer or rate would be NEEDS YOUR CHECK, not outlined.

Step 4 of 6 - Check the numbers: open the J-88 outline. A 'Check numbers against the export row' button shows three rows (hours 12 vs 12, rate $85 vs 85, amount $1,020 vs 1020), each labelled with the text 'Matches'.

Step 5 of 6 - Next week's log: show the fictional billing log for the week of 2026-05-11 with J-88 outcome invoiced and invoice_id INV-241. Show a mock run as of 2026-05-18. J-88 is SKIPPED with text containing 'INV-241' and 'invoiced'. J-91, J-70, and J-94 stay skipped for the same reasons as step 2. Show the sentence 'Logged invoiced work is not listed again.'

Step 6 of 6 - You create the invoice: state the exact sentences 'You create the invoice. Nothing is sent or collected.' and 'Do not add tax or terms not in the export.' Explain that the person creates, holds, or writes off each row in their own invoicing tool, and that nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or marked paid automatically. guided_demo.fictional_data_notice: All jobs, customers, amounts, hours, rates, invoice numbers, and dates on this page are fictional. No real business or customer data is used, and nothing is connected to QuickBooks, Xero, a time tracker, or any other live system.

kit_contents.title: Unbilled Work Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for the weekly run. It covers writing the minimum amount and skip statuses, exporting completed jobs or time entries as CSV with job id, customer, completion date, hours, rate, amount, invoice status, invoice id, and as-of date, removing emails and other columns the workflow does not need, opening last week's billing log, checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading, and the rule that this is an export review, not a live QuickBooks, Xero, or time-tracker connection. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Unbilled Queue Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that runs SKIP RULES FIRST, lists every skip with its reason, ranks remaining rows by oldest completion date first, drafts invoice outlines using only customer, id, date, hours, rate, and amount from the export, and labels CONFIRMED, NEEDS YOUR CHECK, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. It forbids inventing tax or terms, sending an invoice, and recording a payment.

kit_contents.title: Week-to-Week Billing Log Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt for the following week. It reads the previous billing log with the new export, skips rows whose invoice id is now present or whose log outcome is invoiced or write-off, keeps hold rows in the queue with a CONFIRMED note from the log, and forbids sending or marking anything paid.

kit_contents.title: Skip Rules and Minimum Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person sets the minimum amount to bill, statuses that are never billed, and jobs or customers to always skip. It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the prompts. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Billing Log Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (week_of, job, customer, action_taken, outcome, invoice_id, notes) with allowed outcome values invoiced, hold, write-off, already_invoiced, warranty, below_minimum, disputed, and the fictional J-88 invoiced INV-241 row from the guided demo. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Invoice Outline Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before creating an invoice. It confirms that SKIP RULES FIRST ran, that every skip has a reason, that remaining rows are oldest-first, that CONFIRMED hours, rate, and amount match the export row, that labels are separate, that the outline uses only export fields, that tax and terms were not invented, that a blank invoice id was not treated as proof of never billed, and that the person will create, hold, or write off in their own invoicing tool.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Job Export
kit_contents.purpose: The same fictional four-row job CSV used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real job data.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling job and billing exports in AI tools: review data settings, remove emails and phone numbers, do not paste bank or card details, do not invent tax or terms, do not bill warranty or write-off work without the owner's decision, and do not treat a blank invoice id as proof the customer was never billed off-export. It also states that file upload support differs by plan and that nothing is sent, collected, or marked paid automatically.

decision_rules: Write SKIP RULES FIRST and apply it before ranking or drafting any invoice outline.
Skip any row whose invoice_id is present. Show the reason 'invoice_id <id> present'.
Skip any row whose status is in the owner's never-billed list (default warranty, plus owner-marked write-off). Show the reason 'status <status>'.
Skip any row whose amount (or hours x owner rate) is below the owner's minimum. Show the reason 'amount $<amount> is below your $<minimum> minimum'.
Skip any row whose completed date is after the export as-of date. Show the reason 'completed after as-of date'.
Skip any row marked disputed in the export or the billing log. Show the reason 'disputed; needs your decision'.
Skip any job or customer on the owner's always-skip list. Show the reason 'on your always-skip list'.
If a remaining row is missing job id, customer, or both hours-and-rate and amount, do not outline it. List it under NEEDS YOUR CHECK.

If amount is missing and hours and rate are present, compute amount as hours x rate and label the product CONFIRMED from those export fields. If rate is missing, write NEEDS YOUR CHECK. Do not invent a rate.
Rank remaining unbilled rows by oldest completion date first. If two rows share a completion date, larger amount first.
Invoice outlines may state only customer, job or entry id, completed date, hours, rate, and amount from the export row. Do not invent line items, taxes, payment terms, PO numbers, or discounts.
A blank invoice id is CONFIRMED as blank. It is not proof the customer was never billed off-export. That caution is AI INTERPRETATION.
Do not treat Collections follow-up copy as an unbilled outline. This workflow is for work with no invoice id, not for overdue sent invoices.
The outline is a draft only. Do not send it. Do not create the invoice. Do not record a payment. Suggest a billing-log row; the person adds it.
On a later run, start from a new export and the current billing log. Skip rows whose log outcome is invoiced or write-off, or whose invoice id is now present.
human_ai_boundary: AI applies skip rules and lists every skipped row with its reason. The person decides whether a warranty, write-off, or disputed row should still be billed.
AI ranks remaining rows by oldest completion date first. The person decides which outlines to create this week and in what order.
AI drafts invoice outlines using only export fields. The person checks every number against the export row, edits the wording, and approves it.
AI labels a blank invoice id as CONFIRMED blank, not as proof of never billed. The person checks their invoicing tool before creating a duplicate invoice.
AI never sends an invoice, never records a payment, and never edits QuickBooks, Xero, or a time tracker. The person creates, holds, or writes off in their own invoicing tool, or decides not to.
AI reads the billing log. Only the person records outcomes, and the log reflects what the person entered, not what AI assumed.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, collected, or marked paid automatically. Every page states that the person creates the invoice, and that nothing is sent or collected.
Atlas does not connect to QuickBooks, Xero, a time tracker, an invoicing tool, email, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting or uploading exports to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings (such as chat history, training use, and file retention) and to remove emails, phone numbers, and other columns the workflow does not need.
The kit tells the person not to paste bank account numbers, card numbers, or tax IDs into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.

The kit tells the person not to invent tax or terms, not to bill warranty or included-rework without an owner decision, and not to treat a blank invoice id as proof the customer was never billed off-export.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.
The pages contain no statistics, collection rates, savings, ROI claims, prices, or checkout. The only dollar figures are fictional job amounts and the fictional $150 minimum.
required_data_tools: Job, project, or time-entry export (CSV) with completion date, invoice status, and invoice id if any
Owner rate table if the export has hours but no amount
Billing log spreadsheet, started from the kit's Billing Log Template
The owner's own invoicing tool (QuickBooks, Xero, or a spreadsheet) for creating invoices
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; rows can be pasted as text instead.

constraints: Private preview only. The guided demo lives at /blueprints/unbilled-work-review-queue and the Premium kit at /blueprints/unbilled-work-review-queue/kit. Both pages set robots noindex and are not linked from the homepage, header navigation, or the sitemap.

The Premium kit requires requireUser from src/lib/auth.ts and hasActiveEntitlement for this product. It is labelled "Premium · Private preview". It shows no Stripe price, checkout, or Buy Premium unless the product is already in PAID_PRODUCTS.
All sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional. No live connector, OAuth flow, API call, or upload to a third party.
AI prepares; the person decides. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately. Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.
No invented statistics, savings, or ROI claims. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini capabilities differ by plan; say so where it matters.

Product files live in app/blueprints/unbilled-work-review-queue/, components/premium/unbilled-work-review-queue/, and src/lib/premium/unbilled-work-review-queue/. Register the Blueprint in src/lib/blueprints.ts. Do not edit Daily Inbox, Collections product behavior, Stripe, or Production.
e2e/unbilled-work-review-queue/authenticated.spec.ts is read-only once it exists. Do not skip, weaken, or rewrite it. Authenticated QA uses automatic session refresh.
Keyboard accessible, visible labels, no horizontal scrolling at a phone-sized viewport, no console errors.
